Web search results for query: "Yurika Queensland Electric Super Highway charging price per kWh"

Links: [{"title":"Queensland extends the Electric Super Highway - electrive.com","url":"https://www.electrive.com/2021/06/21/queensland-extends-the-electric-super-highway/"},{"title":"Queensland EV charging no longer free - carsales.com.au","url":"https://www.carsales.com.au/editorial/details/queensland-ev-charging-no-longer-free-119547/"},{"title":"EV drivers spend average $3 and 34 minutes charging on electric superhighway","url":"https://thedriven.io/2021/04/09/ev-drivers-spend-average-3-and-34-minutes-charging-on-electric-superhighway/"},{"title":"Queensland EV charging no longer free - Servopro","url":"https://servopro.com.au/queensland-ev-charging-no-longer-free/"},{"title":"Yurika / Electric Highway EV Charger Gunalda, QLD","url":"https://plugroo.com.au/location/yurika-electric-highway-qld-gunalda-42-balkin-street"},{"title":"Queensland to add 13 charging stations to Electric Vehicle Super Highway - The Driven","url":"https://thedriven.io/2020/09/10/queensland-to-add-13-charging-stations-to-electric-vehicle-super-highway/"},{"title":"Yurika EV Charger Esk, QLD","url":"https://plugroo.com.au/location/yurika-electric-highway-qld-esk-pryde-st"},{"title":"RACQ powers up Qld’s Electric Vehicle Superhighway","url":"https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/press-releases/racq-powers-up-qlds-electric-vehicle-superhighway/"}]

Yurika's QESH charging prices have risen a lot since the network launched. The most recent figures I found are from listings about 103 days old.

- **Current (Plugroo listings):**
  - The Gunalda site lists $0.35–0.55 per kWh. That breaks down as $0.35 for the 22 kW Type 2 plugs and $0.55 for the 75 kW fast plugs.
  - The Esk site lists $0.30–0.55 per kWh. That is $0.30 for the 22 kW Type 2 plugs and $0.55 for the 50 kW DC plugs.
  - Plugroo is a third-party aggregator, not an official Yurika source.
- **2020–2021:** The network charged 20 cents per kWh. The average session cost about $3.
- **Earlier still:** The network was free at first. Reports then said a fee of 45 cents per kWh was coming. The Queensland Main Roads Minister said negotiations were underway to charge less than that. The later 20 cent rate matches that.
- **Who sets prices:** Yurika Energy reportedly sets the prices, and Chargefox manages the network.

I didn't find an official Yurika or Queensland Government price page. The Plugroo figures are the best current estimate.
